newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randfontein delays job cuts to end of week.
newsitem.headline: Randfontein delays job cuts to end of week.

text.p: Randfontein Estates Gold Mine Ltd said on Monday that mine management had agreed to postpone any compulsory retrenchments at the mine until the end of the week.

In a statement mine managers JCI Ltd said that Randfontein had agreed to allow the National Union of Mineworkers' (NUM) technical advisor to return to the mine to complete a further report on the need to downscale the mine's workforce.
Randfontein would postpone any job cuts until the end of this week when the technical advisor is expected to present his report, the statement said.
But it said that the process could not be extended indefinitely as the additional costs to the mine, some 300,000 rand per day, jeopardised the jobs of the remainder of the workforce.
"This is the third time that retrenchments have been postponed at Randfontein Estates in an attempt by management to find a mutually agreeable way forward with the NUM," it said.
JCI said on May 28 that it planned to shed a third of Randfontein's 12,000-strong workforce and reduce tonnage throughput as part of a far-reaching restructuring at the struggling gold mine.
JCI said that a further meeting with the NUM had been scheduled for Tuesday morning.

"Management looks forward to resolving the outstanding issues concerning the restructuring of Randfontein Estates as speedily and inclusively as possible in the interest of all stakeholders," the statement said.
It said that management was concerned that the NUM was blocking the process of voluntary retrenchment by witholding the names of workers who wished to accept a severance package.
The NUM had turned down a "generous severance package", JCI said. "Management regards this as a blatant delaying tactic."

Randfontein produced 4,392 kg of gold in the three months to end-March, compared to 5,100 kg previously. It plunged into a 2.86 million rand loss from a 43,83 million rand profit in the preceding quarter.
